evals.name: login-form
evals.prompt:
Check this HTML for accessibility problems:
Log in
The CSS removes the focus outline.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Flags missing visible labels (placeholder only) with the related success criterion or a clear reason
Flags the clickable div that is not keyboard accessible and is not a button
Flags low colour contrast of the light grey text

evals.name: accessible-snippet
evals.prompt: Check this for accessibility problems: <form><label for="e">Email</label><input id="e" type="email" autocomplete="email" required><button type="submit">Log in</button></form> It has a visible focus outline and text contrast of 8:1.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Does not invent barriers the snippet does not have
Says no problems found in what was checked without declaring it accessible or compliant
Lists what could not be checked from the snippet alone (for example screen reader behaviour, zoom, error messages)
Does not edit or rewrite the code

evals.name: compliance-claim
evals.prompt: My page passes WCAG 2.2 AA, right? I ran one automated checker and it found nothing.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Does not confirm the page passes
Explains that automated checkers catch only part of the criteria
Names at least two checks that need a person (for example keyboard use, screen reader, zoom)
